Subject: Greenline demo follow-up: integration ops & schema questions

Thanks again for the demo time today, Samantha — appreciate the walkthrough of your invoice search use case. Quick post-call recap and a short list of integration/architecture questions so our engineering team can size the prototype: 

1) SDK & auth model
- Which environment will you prefer to run from (cloud-hosted app vs VPC service)? That determines whether you want API key per service account or short-lived tokens from your IdP.
- Do you have existing KMS/HSM for secrets we should integrate with for dedicated/private deployments?

2) Routing & model variants
- Expected QPS and peak concurrency (rough numbers) so we can recommend Dedicated vs Hosted with routing policies.

3) Structured output / tool calling
- You mentioned wanting structured invoice extraction + lookup of vendor metadata. We'll propose a tool-calling flow and a JSON schema for the extractor.

4) Embeddings & reranker plan
- Clarify whether you want embeddings for semantic search only (periodic batch) or live reranking on every query. Also sample corpus size would help.

5) Request/response schema items
- For recommendation: chat vs completions (we'll outline tradeoffs), tokenization and how to set max_tokens/stop sequences for reliable extraction, and streaming semantics when using function/tool calling.

Action items:
- I've attached a one-page mutual action plan (greenline-mvp-map.xlsx) and a sample schema (greenline-sample-schema.json).
- Could you confirm environment choice and approximate QPS by EOD Friday so we can prep a technical proposal?

Thanks — I’ll loop in Karthik and Laura for the deeper API/schema details.

—

Thanks Rishi — this is great. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Environment: initial pilot will run from our SaaS platform (hosted), but long-term we want the option to move to a VPC/dedicated setup for PII-sensitive customers.
- QPS: baseline is approx 5 TPS, peak up to ~50 TPS during billing cycles.
- Embeddings: we plan nightly batch embeddings for ~2M documents; reranking should be live at query time (we'd like sub-200ms for rerank decision).

Two quick questions that would accelerate our internal decision: 
A) If we use hosted API during pilot, what authentication mechanism do you recommend for rotating keys and limiting scope per environment?
B) For function/tool calling and streaming, how deterministic is the structured JSON output — can we rely on stop sequences + response schema to avoid partial JSON fragments?

Thanks for the quick details, Samantha — helpful. Karthik & Laura: looping you in for the technical specifics below (Karthik, feel free to paste snippets).

Answers to Samantha’s two points: 
A) Hosted auth recommendation (pilot)
- Start with scoped API keys per environment (dev/stage/prod). Keys can be rotated via our Console and integrated with your secrets manager. For tighter security you can use short-lived OAuth tokens generated by your IdP and federated into Redwood Dedicated when you migrate to VPC.
- We support fine-grained key policies (per-route restrictions) so you can limit which endpoints can call model generation vs embeddings.

B) Determinism for structured output + streaming
- If you need strict JSON outputs for extractor tool-calling, we recommend using the function/tool calling interface (assistant returns a single well-typed function call). That avoids partial JSON fragments.
- Streaming can emit partial tokens for UX, but function results are only returned when complete; if you combine streaming + function calls you get a streaming notice followed by the complete structured payload. In practice, set a conservative max_tokens and use explicit stop sequences around the JSON block for fallbacks.

Open questions for sizing: 
- Can you confirm average document length (words) for your invoice corpus? That informs memory/KV cache sizing.
- Do you plan to store embeddings in your own vector DB, or have us host (we can host during pilot for convenience)?

Attached: greenline-mvp-map.xlsx and greenline-sample-schema.json (sample invoice schema to review).

Rishi

Samantha — quick technical notes and a sample SDK snippet. TL;DR: hosted pilot = scoped API keys + per-route restrictions; streaming + function-calling is safe if you use the function interface for structured output.

SDK snippet (Node.js) for init + short-lived token exchange (example):

/* pseudocode */
const Redwood = require('@redwood/inference');
const client = new Redwood.Client({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY });
// For short-lived token (optional)
const token = await fetch('/internal-token-endpoint').then(r => r.text());
const clientShort = new Redwood.Client({ bearerToken: token });

Routing notes:
- You can tag requests with metadata (region, customer_tier). Our smart routing policy can route >critical to Dedicated pool and others to Hosted.
- Model variants: use a smaller quantized model for embeddings and a higher-quality chat model for extraction. We can configure automatic fallback to cheaper variants if the primary pool is saturated.

Streaming & function/tool calling semantics:
- Streaming emits chunks of text; the SDK exposes an onEvent handler. If the model triggers a function call, the runtime buffers the function arguments and returns them atomically once complete. If you rely on stop sequences to delimit a JSON blob, make sure to include robust validation server-side (we recommend a short JSON schema check as a fallback).

Tokenization & max_tokens guidance:
- Use token counters in the SDK before sending (we provide utilities). For extraction tasks, reserve ~200–400 tokens for the output payload (max_tokens). For long context (multi-page invoices) use our KV cache prefixing so you avoid re-sending repeated boilerplate.

Embeddings/Ranking:
- For 2M documents, we suggest hosting embeddings in your vector DB and calling our embeddings API nightly. For live reranking, compute the initial candidate set with ANN, then call our reranker (lightweight model) with top-N candidates to stay within the 200ms SLA.

Happy to jump on a technical sync Thursday if that helps.

—Karthik
